settings.headline: One architect, on purpose
settings.subtitle: Marlowe Architecture is the solo practice of Elena Marlowe, AIA — modern houses, ADUs and remodels in Austin and the Texas Hill Country. One person designs, draws, permits and walks your project.

settings.headline: Small because the work is personal
settings.body:
After a decade in larger firms, I kept watching designs lose their reasons between the person who drew them and the person who answered for them. So I work alone, with excellent engineers and builders, and I take few projects.

See the houses, what I do, and the journal.

items.title: Shade first
items.text: In Central Texas, the west sun is the brief. Porches, orientation and limestone do the work before machinery does.

items.title: Keep the trees
items.text: A heritage oak is a design partner, not an obstacle. Houses here bend around them.

items.title: Small, well made
items.text: A smaller house with real materials beats a big one with apologies. Size is the budget.

items.title: One accountable person
items.text: You always know who decided, who drew it, and who to call. Me.

items.title: Write it down
items.text: Every decision, drawing and update in your client portal. Houses outlive memories of phone calls.

items.title: Built to be lived in
items.text: Mudrooms, shade at six, a place for boots. Beauty that fails Tuesday morning is not beauty.

items.a: No. Elena, her clients and her houses are fictional. Any resemblance to a real architect is accidental.
It is a Raytha use case: a solo architect's portfolio, services, journal and client portal, built on an open-source .NET CMS, with a kit you can rebuild yourself.

items.q: Where do the images come from?
items.a: Every house drawing, plan and portrait was generated by a script, so nothing here shows a real house or person.
